spanish: Y todo lo que cayere desde el cadáver de ellos sobre él se impurecerá; horno y dos fogones serán derribados; impuros ellos, e impuros serán a ustedes.
grammarChanges: su cadáver → el cadáver de ellos: מִנִּבְלָתָם carries a 3mp suffix ('their' carcass); 'su' does not distinguish a plural possessor from a singular one, so the plural is now stated explicitly.
fogones → dos fogones: וְכִירַיִם is masculine dual; an unmarked Spanish plural loses the paired count, so 'dos' marks it explicitly.

Kept 'serán derribados' plural: תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם share one hophal 3ms verb יֻתָּץ, but 'horno y dos fogones' is a two-item Spanish subject joined by 'y', which Spanish grammar requires to take a plural verb; a singular 'será derribado' would be ungrammatical with that compound subject.
readerNote: Chose the grammatical plural 'serán derribados' because Spanish 'horno y dos fogones' joined by 'y' requires a plural verb, even though the Hebrew hophal יֻתָּץ is singular.
